External links for this lesson. All checked to load from a plain request as of the date this
page was written. (Note: eCFR's own site — ecfr.gov — blocks automated/proxied traffic with a
bot check in this repo's build environment, even though a human browser reaches it fine; the
regulation text quoted in this lesson comes from eCFR's public Versioner API instead, and the
links below use verified-loading mirrors of the same official text.)

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 630.10, current text](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/630.10)**
  — Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute mirror of the general donor eligibility
  requirements quoted throughout this lesson. Use this to check the current text, since
  regulations get amended and the copy in this repo's `sources/` folder is a dated snapshot.

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 630.40, current text](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/630.40)**
  — the deferred-donor notification requirements this lesson quotes for the 8-week notification
  clock. Same use case: check for amendments against the dated snapshot in `sources/`.

- **[Cornell LII: Title 21, Part 630 browse index](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/part-630)**
  — the full donor-eligibility part this lesson's two sections sit inside, including the
  definitions in 630.3 (donor, eligibility, suitability) and the requirements specific to
  apheresis and Source Plasma donors in 630.15, which this director-level lesson doesn't cover
  but which your Quality Analyst will cite directly.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)** — the
  U.S. Government Publishing Office's official, legally authoritative annual CFR archive. Use
  this for the official, dated, legally citable version of a specific year's text — for example,
  to confirm exactly what 630.10 said on the date of a past inspection or donor complaint.

- **[Who Can Donate Blood? Eligibility Requirements Explained | Interview with Dr. Courtney
  Lawrence](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=otspGeTXqe0)** (American Red Cross, from oEmbed
  `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. A real blood-collection organization
  walking through donor-eligibility logic from the donor-facing side; it doesn't mention 630.10,
  BECS, or Lakeshore. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[AABB: About AABB Standards](https://www.aabb.org/standards-accreditation/standards)** —
  AABB's own public page on what its Standards are and how accreditation against them works.
  Useful for keeping this lesson's distinction straight: 630.10 is FDA *regulation*; AABB
  Standards are a separate, voluntary accreditation layer most blood centers also hold
  themselves to. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NHLBI: Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study (REDS)
  Program](https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/science/recipient-epidemiology-and-donor-evaluation-study-reds-program)**
  — where the evidence base behind donor-eligibility policy actually comes from. REDS (now in
  its REDS-IV-P phase) is an NHLBI-funded **research program**, not a regulation, guidance
  document, or AABB Standard — it studies donor and transfusion-recipient safety and sometimes
  informs later FDA or AABB policy changes, but a REDS finding is never itself a citable
  requirement. Read this as research context behind the rule, not as a fifth source to cite
  alongside 630.10. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[IBM: What Is Master Data Management
  (MDM)?](https://www.ibm.com/topics/master-data-management)** — a general explainer on the
  identity-matching and single-source-of-truth problem this lesson's ITSM bridge raises (the
  same shape as a CMDB with two records for one configuration item, applied here to a donor
  record). Not blood-industry-specific — use it to firm up the general MDM concept, then apply
  it to why Thursday's registry check depends on proof of identity, not a name. Verified loading
  via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about donor eligibility and why screening is risk-based.

- **[080CE: Is This Donor "Safe?" with Mindy Goldman](https://www.bbguy.org/2020/02/27/080/)** (Blood Bank Guy podcast, Joe Chaffin) — a practitioner conversation on how donor eligibility questions get designed and why a deferral is a risk judgment, not a moral one. Good background for why the Donor History Questionnaire is not something IT can casually change. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[084: COVID-19 Convalescent Plasma with Pampee Young and Ralph Vassallo](https://www.bbguy.org/2020/05/04/084/)** (Blood Bank Guy podcast) — a case study in how a blood center recruits and qualifies a special donor population fast, and the operational records that depend on it. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[BBGuy Podcast Archives](https://www.bbguy.org/category/podcast/)** (Blood Bank Guy) — the full episode list with transcripts for many episodes; skim titles to build blood-banking vocabulary, and a useful starting point if you later consider the ASCP SBB (Specialist in Blood Banking) path. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
